turns.content: Divide R=[0,2]x[0,2] into four equal squares. What are Delta x, Delta y, and the area Delta A of each subrectangle?
List the upper-right-corner sample point for each of the four subrectangles in a consistent order.
For those four points, tabulate x^2 and y^2 separately so the surface heights can be evaluated without changing the point order.
Use the first-order Taylor linearization of the surface about (0,0) as the sole height-evaluation method at all four sample points.
Multiply each sampled height by Delta A and add the four contributions to obtain the Riemann-sum volume estimate.

Using the signs of the partial derivatives on R, determine whether each upper-right sample is a cell minimum or maximum and whether the estimate is below or above the true volume, without evaluating the exact integral.
Check that every cell contribution has volume units and use the cellwise height comparison to verify the direction of the inequality for the total estimate.
Report the final upper-right-corner Riemann-sum estimate for the volume and state its inequality relative to the true volume.
